newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada junior oil company stocks jump on prospects.
newsitem.headline: Canada junior oil company stocks jump on prospects.

text.p: Hot prospects for two Canadian junior oil companies have lured investors in droves, driving up their stock prices in busy volumes.
Shares of Remington Energy Ltd, jumped C$3 to 21.25 in Toronto on Friday on the potential for multi-zone oil and gas discoveries in northeastern British Columbia.
Several analysts said Remington's price had left their 12-month targets in the dust. Last week, Remington was trading at 14.
Another small firm, Maxx Petroleum Ltd climbed as high as 2.80 early on Friday, up from 1.85 on January 10.
The stock settled back to 2.69, up 0.19, in late trade on volume of 1.5 million shares.
Remington said on Friday it had bought 26 sections of land near its West Stoddart play near Fort St. John at Thursday's B.C. land sale.
In a release issued at the request of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Remington did not disclose the price of the acreage.

However, several industry sources said the company paid a rich C$13.5 million for the land, which was said to include its top exploration prospects and a well drilled several years ago which flowed oil but was never abandoned.
Remington posted a C$200,000 bond for abandonment liabilities for the well, analysts said.
Matt Janisch, analyst with Nesbitt Burns, said he raised his target price for Remington twice in the past week, on Friday upping it to 24 from 20.

Janisch said wells in the area had the potential to strike oil reserves in the Doig geological formation and there was also potential for gas which could produce at over 10 million cubic feet per day.
"The area is hydrocarbon supercharged," he said.
Earlier this week, Remington was boosted by news that its West Stoddart facility was at full capacity and unable to handle full production of extremely light oil from the field.
It said the facility wpould be expanded to 9,000 barrels of oil and gas liquids per day and five additional horizontal locations would be drilled through spring.

Meanwhile, Maxx president and chief executive Burl Aycock said his firm was near announcing the results of two recently completed wells, one in southeastern Saskatchewan and another in southern Alberta.
Maxx also plans to begin drilling before the end of the first quarter in Kansas, where it has amassed a large land position, Aycock said.
He also said he believed investors were reacting positively to the company's 1996 performance, which exceeded expections.
